## Kessler family gives $20 million toward children's behavioral health hospital

LINCOLN, Neb. -- The Kessler Family Foundation has given $20 million to Prairie Bend Health toward a $64 million, 48-bed psychiatric hospital for children and adolescents, the largest gift in the system's 110-year history.

The Kessler Children's Behavioral Health Hospital will be built on the Prairie Bend Medical Center campus and is expected to open in 2029. Funding includes the Kessler gift, a $12 million grant from the state, $28 million from PBH and $4 million from other donors.

"My father grew up in Beatrice and never forgot how far families had to go for help. Our family is proud to help bring this care home," said Ruth Kessler, a trustee of the Kessler Family Foundation.

"[Governor quote: pending Office of the Governor]"

"Nebraska families wait too long, and travel too far, for psychiatric care for their children," said Dr. Raymond Ellison, PBH president and CEO. "This gift changes that."

Today, children who need inpatient psychiatric care in southeast Nebraska are often sent out of state; PBH has no pediatric psychiatric beds.

# Statement to The Prairie Ledger (DRAFT v1 for Steven Pike and Nora Calloway)

Attributable to Prairie Bend Health:

"Federal privacy law does not allow us to confirm whether someone was a patient or to discuss anyone's care without their authorization. We take every concern about care seriously, and when a concern is raised we review the care provided.

Our emergency department is busier than ever: 6,840 visits in October, up 9% from a year ago. In October, the median time from arrival to being seen by a provider was 34 minutes. Since July we have hired 22 emergency nurses, added six travel nurses for respiratory season and, since Oct. 15, added a second triage nurse on evening shifts. Like hospitals across the country, we are still recruiting: 14 of our 118 emergency nursing positions are open.

Anyone with a concern about their care or a family member's care can contact Patient Relations at 402-555-0190."

# All-staff email from Dr. Raymond Ellison (send Thursday, Nov. 5, 10:05 a.m. CT, not before). Subject: The largest gift in our history

Dear colleagues,

A few minutes ago, with Gov. Patricia Hartley, Ruth Kessler and the Garcia family, we announced the largest gift in Prairie Bend Health's 110-year history. The Kessler Family Foundation has given $20 million toward the Kessler Children's Behavioral Health Hospital, a 48-bed psychiatric hospital for children and adolescents that we will build on the Prairie Bend Medical Center campus. With a $12 million grant from the state, $28 million from PBH and $4 million from other donors, the $64 million project is fully funded. We expect to break ground in spring 2027 and open in 2029.

Today, when a child in southeast Nebraska needs inpatient psychiatric care, we too often have to send them out of state. Many of you have made those calls and comforted those families. This hospital will let us care for those children here, close to home.

None of this happens without you. Our caregivers, in every department and especially in an emergency department that is busier than ever, are the reason families trust us. Thank you.

If a reporter contacts you, please refer them to the media line at 402-555-0110.

Ray

# Media brief: Dr. Leah Morrow, Medical Director, Child and Adolescent Psychiatry (embargoed until 10 a.m. CT Thu Nov. 5)

Your role: the clinician who explains what the new hospital will mean for children and families. Interviews Thursday after 1 p.m., and follow-ups next week.

Three messages:
1. Children in southeast Nebraska who need inpatient psychiatric care are often sent out of state; PBH has no pediatric psychiatric beds today.
2. The Kessler Children's Behavioral Health Hospital will have 48 beds on the PBMC campus, opening in 2029, so families can stay involved in their child's care.
3. Help is available now: talk to your child's doctor, and anyone in crisis can call or text 988.

Facts: $64 million project ($20 million Kessler gift, $12 million state grant, $28 million PBH, $4 million other donors); groundbreaking spring 2027.

Likely questions: How many Nebraska kids go out of state? (If you don't have a sourced number, say so.) How will you staff it? (Recruiting and training starts in 2027.) What will a stay look like? Why not outpatient care instead? (Both are needed.)

Logistics: I'll be with you for every interview; TV likes 8-12 second answers; look at the reporter, not the camera.
